subject: Cross-zone prompt sandbox & load windows — POC kickoff scheduling
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@finsecure.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cross-zone prompt sandbox & load windows — POC kickoff scheduling

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for agreeing to a hands-on POC. To make the kickoff efficient for your engineers across regions, I sketched three 90-minute windows we can rotate through so each region can join at a reasonable local hour and we can run an end-to-end prompt review + routing check and one short load test.

Proposed rotation windows (examples; all times listed local / UTC):
- US window: 2027-01-12 09:00–10:30 PST (17:00–18:30 UTC) — prompt review + routing sanity checks
- EU window: 2027-01-12 14:00–15:30 CET (13:00–14:30 UTC) — hands-on prompt tuning & token accounting
- APAC window: 2027-01-13 19:00–20:30 HKT (11:00–12:30 UTC) — live load rehearsal (short 15–20m ramp)

What I need from you to lock the slots:
- Preferred 1–2 windows to prioritize (we can iterate)
- A primary technical contact for each region (names + emails)
- Any blackouts (legal reviews, holiday blocks) so we avoid conflicts

Attachments: I attached a rotation matrix with suggested owners and a short load-test plan (crosszone-rotation-matrix.csv, load-test-plan.pdf). Also included a small prompt set for the initial review (prompt_review_set_v2.csv).

If those examples look good I can publish calendar invites (separate invites per window) and include an agenda: 10m kick-off, 40m prompt + routing walkthrough, 20m short load rehearsal, 20m triage & next steps.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee

+1 (415) 555-0172

Thanks for the quick reply, Samantha.

Based on your availability I updated the rotation matrix and attached a small suggested sequence: start with the US block on Tue Jan 12 at 09:00 PST for the baseline prompt review, then run the EU slot later the same day (14:00 CET) for routing validation, and hold the APAC rehearsal on Thu Jan 14 as a single concentrated session.

Note: Legal flagged a short review window on the 12th morning; to be safe I moved the official calendar invites 30 minutes later and marked them tentative. If that conflicts with your team, we can shift back.

Proposed concrete invites (links below) — I can publish these and include dial-ins and steps for the short load rehearsal:
- US window (tentative): 2027-01-12 09:30–11:00 PST — https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcd1234
- EU window (confirmed): 2027-01-12 15:00–16:30 CET — https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=efgh5678
- APAC rehearsal: 2027-01-14 19:00–20:30 HKT — https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=ijkl9012

Action items for us (Redwood):
- Finalize rotation matrix and publish invites (Soojin)
- Prep a short prompt checklist for the US session (Tessa)
- Confirm capacity for a 20m ramp to 50 concurrent connections during the rehearsal (Marcus)

I attached the updated csv for the rotation matrix. Let me know if the 09:30 PST start is an issue — happy to move it earlier if your team prefers.

— Soojin

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@finsecure.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-zone prompt sandbox & load windows — POC kickoff scheduling

Soojin — quick ops note (cc-ing Samantha for transparency).

We should constrain the load rehearsal parameters so we don’t trigger autoscaling during the initial POC:
- Target steady-state: 25 concurrent connections (short 20s requests), 15–20k tokens/min aggregate
- Short ramp: 90s ramp to 50 concurrent for 3–5 minutes, then fall back to steady-state
- Max request size limit for rehearsal: 1024 tokens; recommend using the prompt_review_set_v2.csv trimmed to 512 tokens per prompt to reduce variability

Lauren, can you confirm we have a dedicated pool that will hold this load without cross-customer bleed? If not, we should set a conservative backstop and inform FinSecure so they know expected latency behavior during the rehearsal.
